verdict.rationale_short: June CPI printed -0.4% MoM / 3.5% YoY — exactly at the morning's BUY gate — and July Fed hike probability collapsed from 40%+ to 20%. Tech and crypto rallied: NVDA +3.7%, BTC Gate 2 reset at $64,434. But the 30Y barely moved (5.097% vs 5.101%), Russell declined -0.83% despite the broad rally, and IBM's -25% crash (enterprise software budgets redirecting to AI hardware) is a new cross-sector risk for tomorrow. AI hardware and crypto are clear buys on dips; enterprise software and small caps are not.

bear_case: Counter-thesis: today's CPI print was the most bullish macro data point in six weeks. Core CPI at 2.6% YoY (vs 2.9% consensus) and headline -0.4% MoM are not soft prints — they are disinflationary surprise events that eliminate July hike as a credible scenario and recalibrate market pricing. Goldman Sachs posted its best quarter in history; JPMorgan profits jumped 41%; bank earnings season is constructive. BTC Gate 2 was reset decisively at $64,434. IBM's warning is an outlier in a strong quarter — one company shifting its product narrative, not a signal that AI hardware demand is collapsing (the shift to hardware spending from software is explicitly bullish for NVDA/AMD/AVGO). The 30Y at 5.097% is a lagged indicator; the front-end move (2Y -14bps) is the leading signal, and historically front-end rallies precede long-end rallies by 3-8 weeks. The HOLD verdict may be premature conservatism. Invalidation: if SPX fails to hold above 7,500 by Friday close with VIX re-engaging above 17, today's rally was a dead-cat bounce in a deteriorating trend.
